## Structure and components

- [statement] The authors of the phase 2 lixisenatide trial report that at 12 months MDS-UPDRS part III scores had changed by -0.04 points with lixisenatide and 3.04 points with placebo (difference, 3.08; 95% confidence interval, 0.86 to 5.30; P = 0.007). (high confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38598572/ · keywords: GLP-1 agonists and drug repurposing in PD · also: https://www.michaeljfox.org/news/results-parkinsons-trial-diabetes-drug-lixisenatide-published
- [statement] A 2017 phase II exenatide trial of 62 patients treated for 48 weeks reported a mean 3.5-point advantage over placebo in off-medication MDS-UPDRS part III scores, assessed at 60 weeks. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28781108/ · keywords: GLP-1 agonists and drug repurposing in PD · also: https://www.medpagetoday.com/neurology/parkinsonsdisease/114113

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Exenatide-PD3 was a phase 3, multicentre, double-blind, parallel-group, randomised, placebo-controlled trial at six research hospitals in the UK that randomly assigned 194 participants to extended-release exenatide 2 mg once per week over 96 weeks or placebo. (high confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39919773/ · keywords: GLP-1 agonists and drug repurposing in PD · also: https://cureparkinsons.org.uk/2025/02/exenatide-pd3-results-published/
- [statement] In the phase 2 lixisenatide trial, the authors report nausea in 46% and vomiting in 13% of participants receiving lixisenatide, and MJFF adds that more than a third needed a reduced dose. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38598572/ · keywords: GLP-1 agonists and drug repurposing in PD · also: https://www.michaeljfox.org/news/results-parkinsons-trial-diabetes-drug-lixisenatide-published

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] The authors of the phase 3 exenatide trial state that they found no evidence to support exenatide as a disease-modifying treatment for people with Parkinson's disease, and that exenatide was safe and well tolerated. (high confidence) (verified as of 2025-02-04) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39919773/ · keywords: GLP-1 agonists and drug repurposing in PD · also: https://www.michaeljfox.org/news/exenatide-glp-1-drug-shows-no-impact-parkinsons-symptoms
- [statement] A Lancet Expression of Concern now qualifies the published exenatide disease-modification trial: the trial authors report no evidence of benefit, while the Lancet notice says the impact of regulatory inspection findings on the study data and reported conclusions is still being assessed. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39919773/ · keywords: GLP-1 agonists and drug repurposing in PD · also: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42330995/, https://www.parkinsonsdisease.blog/exenatide-again/, https://www.thelancet.com/action/showPdf?pii=S0140-6736%2826%2901241-9
- [statement] A phase 2, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial of daily subcutaneous lixisenatide or placebo for 12 months, followed by a 2-month washout period, enrolled 156 participants diagnosed with Parkinson's disease less than 3 years earlier. (high confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38598572/ · keywords: GLP-1 agonists and drug repurposing in PD · also: https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT03439943?format=json, https://www.michaeljfox.org/news/results-parkinsons-trial-diabetes-drug-lixisenatide-published
- [statement] The stated repurposing rationale for GLP-1 receptor agonists in Parkinson's disease is neurotrophic or neuroprotective effects in preclinical models, plus epidemiological studies and small randomised trials suggesting possible benefit. (high confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39919773/ · keywords: GLP-1 agonists and drug repurposing in PD · also: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28781108/, https://www.michaeljfox.org/news/exenatide-glp-1-drug-shows-no-impact-parkinsons-symptoms
- [statement] The authors of the phase 3 exenatide trial write that agents with better target engagement, or studies in specific subgroups of patients, are needed to establish whether GLP-1 receptor agonists have any support in Parkinson's disease, and MJFF likewise says carefully controlled study populations could reveal groups who respond better. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2025-02-04) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39919773/ · keywords: GLP-1 agonists and drug repurposing in PD · also: https://www.michaeljfox.org/news/exenatide-glp-1-drug-shows-no-impact-parkinsons-symptoms

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] MJFF states that trials of other drugs in the same class, including NLY01 and PT320, reported no meaningful effect, and MedPage Today reports that the pegylated exenatide analogue NLY01 found no overall benefit compared with placebo but suggested benefits in younger patients. (low confidence) — https://www.michaeljfox.org/news/results-parkinsons-trial-diabetes-drug-lixisenatide-published · keywords: GLP-1 agonists and drug repurposing in PD · also: https://www.medpagetoday.com/neurology/parkinsonsdisease/114113

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The authors of the exenatide trial report that at 96 weeks MDS-UPDRS III OFF-medication scores, the primary outcome, worsened by a mean of 5.7 points with exenatide and 4.5 points with placebo. (high confidence) (verified as of 2025-02-06) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39919773/ · keywords: GLP-1 agonists and drug repurposing in PD · also: https://www.medpagetoday.com/neurology/parkinsonsdisease/114113
- [statement] The Lancet notice says that on May 18, 2026 it was made aware of regulatory inspection findings at King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust, one of the trial sites, which identified department-wide concerns relating to trial conduct, oversight, and governance, including findings classified by regulators as critical and major. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.parkinsonsdisease.blog/exenatide-again/ · keywords: GLP-1 agonists and drug repurposing in PD · also: https://www.clinicaltrialvanguard.com/article/intel-brief/gcp-breakdown-at-kings-college-hospital-just-clouded-the-most-promising-parkinsons-trial-in-years/, https://www.thelancet.com/action/showPdf?pii=S0140-6736%2826%2901241-9
- [statement] In the phase 2 lixisenatide trial the authors report that other results for the secondary end points did not differ substantially between groups, and MJFF notes that patient-reported secondary measures did not confirm the slowing seen on motor measures. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38598572/ · keywords: GLP-1 agonists and drug repurposing in PD · also: https://www.michaeljfox.org/news/results-parkinsons-trial-diabetes-drug-lixisenatide-published
- [statement] As of the registry record's last update on 2026-05-06, the registry lists NCT04232969, the exenatide phase PHASE3 trial, as COMPLETED, with a start date of 2020-01-20 and 194 actual participants. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT04232969?format=json · keywords: GLP-1 agonists and drug repurposing in PD

## Research summary — GLP-1 agonists and drug repurposing in PD

GLP-1 receptor agonists, developed for diabetes, were tested in Parkinson's disease after preclinical neuroprotection findings and small trials. A single-centre exenatide phase II trial and a phase 2 lixisenatide trial reported motor benefits. The larger exenatide phase 3 trial reported no evidence of disease modification at 96 weeks. The Lancet later issued an Expression of Concern on that paper after a regulatory inspection at a trial site, with an investigation pending. Open issues are phase 2 to phase 3 translation, target engagement and subgroup selection.

## Source disagreement — GLP-1 agonists and drug repurposing in PD

The 2017 exenatide phase II trial reported a motor advantage, whereas the authors of the later phase 3 exenatide trial report no evidence of disease modification.

## Open question — GLP-1 agonists and drug repurposing in PD

Whether GLP-1 agents other than exenatide, such as semaglutide, change progression in Parkinson's disease; MedPage Today notes ongoing semaglutide trials.
